answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, require each agent to grow a public vine of sequential work receipts: every new leaf is a cipher of the prior leaf, a unique nonce, and a time window that cannot be ground in parallel. Admission software then compares vines and rejects any newcomer whose history is a mirror of an existing prefix, because that clone copied rather than recomputed the chain. An attacker who wants many identities must therefore spend N times the delayed work; pasting someone else's cipher or splicing leaves fails the mirror check and slashes the stake posted to open the vine.
